children: Higher interest rates are likely to weigh more heavily on Saudi Arabia's credit growth than the U.A.E.'s, Emirates NBD Research says. Saudi inflation remains below 2%, raising inflation-adjusted borrowing costs as lending growth slows. In contrast, higher U.A.E. inflation, partly reflecting more market-sensitive food and energy prices, has kept real borrowing costs lower, while credit growth has recovered from its spring slowdown. Both countries' dollar pegs require rates to broadly track U.S. policy. Emirates NBD expects another Federal Reserve rate increase this year, followed by a prolonged pause through much of 2027, leaving Saudi borrowers more exposed to tighter financial conditions. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)
